next_up: Step 4 (deep design): the STORY, one subject at a time — player thread (§2) -> each NPC's story brief (§3) -> the world (§5) -> reactivity-as-experience (§4). STORY only, no structure.
Order is enforced: don't start the NPC briefs until the PLAYER thread is done.
BUDGET, stated at casting so the blueprint cannot quietly shrink it: ~93-133 NPC canvases + ~30-40 player track = ~125-170 total. v1 shipped 76. That is what 'own the whole household' costs.

decisions_log.decision: RE-AUTHOR, not a patch. v1 archived at archive/the_inheritance_v1/ (book rev 72) and de-listed from games-data.js (it was live on the GitHub Pages portal). Borrow Steps 0-4 as raw material; generate Step 5 (blueprint) onward FRESH.
decisions_log.why: v1's premise/cast/map/machine are good (the skill cites its map by name as canonical). Its failures are entirely below the blueprint: 47% one-shot canvases, 7 Lane-2 ambients in the whole game (Audrey: zero), 8 Lane-3 walk-ins re-registered 41x, NPCs scheduled into rooms with no canvases, 88/102 nodes with no choice. Importing the v1 blueprint would import the corridor.

LO's call. RTS-native, the skill's default, and what v1 already wrote well ('You draw the curtain and lie down in the room you grew up in'). Explicitly NOT Vesper's third person, which drifted literary and shipped 'You:' labels over 'she' prose. Mirror as [settings] narration_person = "second" at authoring.

decisions_log.decision: Fantasy KEPT as-is from v1 (Mode A, LO chose 'keep it').
decisions_log.why: Clears the 3-part bar: POV-fit (female-PC takeover from within), sharp charge (power-reversal + incest taboo, conquest not longing), built-in two acts (take the hotel as leverage -> pick them off). The specific wound (Eleanor chose her second family, then died before any reckoning was possible) is what lifts it above the generic 'inherit the house' category.

decisions_log.decision: Systems: clothing YES, phone YES, money-as-CONTROL-economy YES, player_portrait YES.
decisions_log.why: First three carried from v1 unchanged. The player portrait is NEW (engine feature shipped 2026-07-06, after v1 was written) — LO's call to include it: the game has clothing, a customizable PC, and a corruption spine, which is exactly what the portrait's three axes feed on, and 'watch yourself become someone else' is the game's whole spine. Cost acknowledged: ~15-30 consistent images, sourced at authoring.

decisions_log.decision: Two cast holes flagged for Step 3 (casting) to close.
decisions_log.why: v1 gave the money pressure NO FACE (its banker was 3 one-shots and an empty bank room) and let Lorna die after 4 beats despite her being the mentor the whole player-corruption track hangs on. Margaret also needs ~3x her v1 canvas count or she is not an apex.

decisions_log.decision: FAIL-STATE: none, by design (LO's call, Mode A). Nothing is ever confiscated.
decisions_log.why: Declared, not defaulted. CONSEQUENCE, and it is load-bearing: v1's foreclosure clock is CUT, not softened — the skill cites this game BY NAME as its example of 'an advertised threat that could never bite' (step-2-toplevel.md). Pressure is rebuilt from desire instead: the hotel's decline is an OPPORTUNITY (a lever on the floor), and Margaret is a RACE you are visibly losing in your mother's house — the negative axis is STATUS, never property. Pressure escalates by raising the PRIZE, never the danger. Also forces [settings.rent] OFF — turning it on would smuggle the cut fail-state back in through the engine.

decisions_log.decision: BODY-STATE: pregnancy IN, as a late/frontier axis (LO's call, Mode A).
decisions_log.why: v1 flagged it as an open gap and never resolved it across 72 revisions. It lands where the charge already points — Grayson (blood half-brother: the breeding taboo) and Richard (the widower: she replaces Eleanor in the house, so 'becoming the new woman of the house' stops being a metaphor). Rides the engine's existing pregnancy axis (player-portrait pregnancy_suffix + a hidden trait). LAW: always a payoff she CHOOSES, never a punishment — a punitive pregnancy would smuggle the cut fail-state back in.

decisions_log.decision: Borrowed from v1 largely intact: cascade + double lock, stat set, desire ladder, reactive world (incl. the act-scoped FORCED prey-early mode), economy-as-corruption-ladder, THE MACHINE (Margaret's power routed THROUGH Richard + Grayson), pacing, frontier. No renown meter (v1 killed it; stays dead).
decisions_log.why: v1's Step 2 was genuinely good — its failures were all below the blueprint. Re-run through the gates rather than re-invented. ONE clarification v1 never wrote down: exhibitionism vs worn_corruption are NOT duplicates — the outfit is a DIAL you can turn back, exhibitionism is a RATCHET that only climbs. Without that stated, exhibitionism reads as a dead stat and someone cuts it.

decisions_log.decision: §8 declarations written (v1 predated all three): the opening/cold-start, the systems on/off list, the fail-state.
decisions_log.why: Opening = you walk into the lobby and Margaret is behind YOUR MOTHER'S front desk giving orders to her staff — the whole game in one frame (the house is being taken, and not by you). First want: 'Get your hands on this place.' Systems ON: clothing, phone, player portrait, customization. OFF: rent.

decisions_log.decision: Nested-zones, DENSE/LIVING, 21 rooms, every one with a stated job. Free movement inside the building; TIME cost on the single Town<->Lobby bridge. Articled house style, applied evenly.
decisions_log.why: v1's map was not dead, it was LOPSIDED: Audrey's Room 19 canvases vs Grayson's 1, Richard's 3, and MARGARET'S (the apex) 3; the Private Floor (the endgame venue) 1. Three rooms (The Residence, The Grand Stair, Town) had ZERO canvases and v1 declared no containers — so the player could walk into all three and find nothing. The Dining Room was gated on hotel_dining_reopened, a flag set ZERO times in the entire game: unreachable forever, shipped anyway. Topology was never the problem; JOBS were. CUT the Dining Room + Out & About. Gave real jobs to the three empty stages: the Grand Stair = the threshold between her two selves (off-shift in a bold outfit, meeting family coming down); The Residence = the presence/landing surface (npc_at_location: occupied bath, peek, caught); Town = the street's DIFFERENT place ceiling. The Boutique gets a MIRROR — v1 bought the reactive dial and never dramatized turning it. Travel: charging her to climb her own stairs is friction with no drama; the Town cost is what makes schedules bite (leaving the building = missing someone in it).

decisions_log.decision: Cast LOCKED: 4 core targets (Audrey, Margaret, Grayson, Richard) + Lorna (ally, NOT a target, light) + 2 props (Danny, Halloway). MARGARET AND GRAYSON RE-SHAPED antagonist -> family/ambient (dense).
decisions_log.why: THE ROOT CAUSE OF V1, FOUND: Margaret was not under-built — she was MIS-CAST and then built correctly to the wrong budget. v1 cast her 'antagonist' (budget 6-10) and shipped 8 — INSIDE budget. But antagonist/witness is the shape for an obstacle who NEVER BECOMES A TARGET, and she is the game's APEX CONQUEST. An apex needs a climb; 6-10 canvases cannot carry one. Same error on Grayson (cast antagonist, built 14). Both are family/ambient dense (25-35) — they live in the house, they're in front of you constantly, and they are the last two things you take. Grayson's density lives in LANE 3 (he is the in-house face of the forced/prey-early mode), not in a seduction ladder.

decisions_log.decision: MAP AMENDMENT (done whole): Halloway & Sons CUT. 21 -> 20 rooms. Halloway demoted to a one-scene prop (reads the will).
decisions_log.why: His v1 hook read, verbatim, 'Charge: none — he's the deadline with a face.' Step 2 cut the deadline (no fail-state), so he became a roleless NPC — and the taxonomy says roleless = cut or merge. A room whose only inhabitant is a prop fails the room-content floor. The will now lives ENTIRELY under the roof: READ in the Drawing Room (Margaret already in your mother's chair — the opening frame), SIGNED in the Study (Richard, at his own desk, after you've hollowed him out), CONTESTED by Margaret in your face. More on-fantasy, not less: the premise is 'every person under its roof', and the lawyer was the one person who wasn't. LO's call (one-scene prop).

decisions_log.decision: Pressure source = MARGARET (not a banker). Corrupting on-ramp = LORNA.
decisions_log.why: With no fail-state, the pressure-source role cannot be a squeeze that TAKES things. It is a RIVAL who is beating you, visibly, in your mother's house — status pressure, not confiscation. Margaret holds pressure source + late-act pressure + apex target. Structural coverage holds: pressure ✓ on-ramp ✓ core targets ✓ late-act ✓.
